items.title: Host with an existing community
description: The Lab is designed to plug into the groups you already spend time with—whether that's your sorority or fraternity, consulting club, basketball team, or a cappella group.
Instead of starting from scratch, it's best to invite the people you already know or co-host with a community you're part of. Familiar faces create better conversations.
items.brainstormQuestion: What group do you already spend time with that might be curious about AI?

inputs.label: Community or group you'll host with

items.title: Pick a theme
description: People are using ChatGPT for all sorts of things—studying, applying to jobs, cooking, working out, creativity, you name it.
So it's best to pick a theme that's relevant and exciting to your group. It'll help keep the conversation focused.
items.brainstormQuestion: What topic would get your group most excited to explore together?

items.title: Decide what you'll share
description: This event is meant to share ideas from many students, so we recommend inviting others to share how they're using ChatGPT alongside you.
We've found that having at least 5 presenters works best. It's most effective if they actively show off how they use it in a live or interactive way—not just describe it.
Start thinking about who you might invite. You'll lock that in during logistical planning. For now, decide what _you'll_ share.
items.brainstormQuestion: How do you use ChatGPT in a way that others might find useful or surprising?

items.title: Choose a guiding question
description: The event isn't just about learning new ways to use ChatGPT—it's also about thinking about the larger impacts of AI.
It's good to pair your theme with one deep question to pose after the demos, so people can reflect on what they just saw.
This could be tightly related to your theme so people leave with a holistic perspective, or it could be more general to just spark conversation.
items.brainstormQuestion: What question about AI would you want your group thinking about after they leave?

items.title: Plan how you'll capture it
description: Your event will be one of many happening across the country. We want to highlight what you've done and share it with the broader Lab community so everyone can learn from each other.

The best way to do this is to take a group selfie, snap a few candid shots, or even record parts of it. This can be a great way to get recognition for what you're building on your campus—we might even share your work on OpenAI's social channels.
items.brainstormQuestion: How might you document the event so you can share it afterward?

inputs.label: Your plan for capturing the event
